summary.text: Kelly Morrison is the Democratic incumbent in Minnesota's 3rd Congressional District. An obstetrician-gynecologist who practiced in Minnesota for more than 20 years, she served in the Minnesota House and Senate from 2019 to 2024 before winning the open congressional seat in 2024. She serves on the House Veterans' Affairs and Small Business committees.

paragraphs.text: Born in Minneapolis in 1969. According to her House website, she is a sixth-generation Minnesotan.
Earned a bachelor's degree in history from Yale University and an M.D. from Case Western Reserve University, and completed her residency in obstetrics and gynecology at Northwestern University.
Worked as a physician; her House website says she practiced as an OB-GYN in Minnesota for more than 20 years.
Won election to the Minnesota House of Representatives (District 33B) in 2018, defeating incumbent Cindy Pugh 50.4% to 49.5%, and served from 2019 to 2023.
Served in the Minnesota Senate from 2023 to 2024, with committee assignments that included Health and Human Services Finance and Policy and Transportation Finance and Policy (vice chair).

According to her House website, she passed more than 90 bills in six years in the state legislature and received awards from groups including the Minnesota Psychiatric Society and the National Alliance on Mental Illness.
Elected to the U.S. House on November 5, 2024, defeating Republican Tad Jude 58.4% to 41.5% in the open seat previously held by Dean Phillips (D).

In the 119th Congress, assigned to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs (Disability Assistance and Memorial Affairs) and the Committee on Small Business (Contracting and Infrastructure; Rural Development, Energy, and Supply Chains).
According to her House website, she and her husband, John Willoughby, a former Army Ranger, have three children.
